docs.title: Privacy notice
docs.summary: Junkyard Draft has no accounts, no e-mail sign-up, no cookies and no advertising. The game keeps your settings and best scores on your device. The verifier keeps what public leaderboards need: the replays you submit, the display name you choose and a hash of a key your device made. You can download or delete all of it from the game, and nothing identifies you to us beyond that key.

sections.title: Who is responsible
items: The data controller is Jon (GitHub: blickz55), living in the United States, who operates Junkyard Draft at https://junkyarddraft.com. Contact for anything in this notice: contact@junkyarddraft.com.
This notice covers the game at junkyarddraft.com, the desktop edition (which talks to the same verifier) and the verifier at verify.junkyarddraft.com. It was last changed on 2026-10-30.

sections.title: On your device
items: The game stores in your browser's local storage (the desktop edition: under your user profile): your settings (sound, text size, motion, resolution, the play-data switch), the current save, your local best scores by rules version, the days you played, a random 128-bit device key with the display name and tag you chose, the group code you joined, the daily reminder's hour and subscription address if you turned it on, and, only while play statistics are on, a random install id with the events not yet sent.

Nothing on your device is sent anywhere except as the next section describes. Clearing the site's data in your browser removes all of it; "Delete my data" in the game replaces the device key and removes the name, the group code and the statistics state, and leaves your local scores and settings alone.

sections.title: What the verifier stores, and why
items: Verified entries. When you submit a run, the verifier stores the replay (seed, your actions, the rules version), the score, the time, the label you chose, the replay's hash and, when you have claimed a name, your player id. Purpose: public leaderboards whose scores were re-simulated rather than trusted. Legal basis: the agreement you enter by submitting (the terms and the fairness policy) and the legitimate interest in boards that are correct.

Your identity. A player id, which is the SHA-256 hash of the key your device created, and the display name and tag you chose with the time of your last rename. The key itself leaves your device only as a bearer header over TLS to the verifier, which hashes it before any use and never stores or logs it. Purpose: one best entry per player, renames that follow you onto every board, groups, and deletion. Legal basis: the agreement.
Groups. The codes of the groups you joined (at most 5), keyed by player id. Purpose: boards scoped to the people you chose. Legal basis: the agreement.

Moderation. Reports you file (your player id, the reported player, one reason from a fixed list, the time), reports filed about your name, and every moderator action on a name (hide, confirm, clear, forced rename) in an audit log. Purpose: names fit for a public board. Legal basis: the legitimate interest in a safe service.

Request logs. One line per request with the method, path, status, duration and a hash of your network address salted with the day, so the same address cannot be followed from one day to the next. The address itself is not written: the reverse proxy in front of the verifier is configured to drop it from its access log as well. Purpose: abuse limits and debugging. Legal basis: the legitimate interest in a service that stays up. Kept by rotation, 7 files of 20 MB each per service, which is days to weeks depending on traffic.

Play statistics, on unless you turn them off. Events from a fixed list of 25 names (which lesson step you reached, that a game completed, that a share was copied, and the like), a random install id stored on your device, and the same daily-salted address hash. Never seeds other than daily and tutorial labels, never layouts, never your player id. Purpose: seeing where the game confuses people, so it can be fixed. Legal basis: the legitimate interest in a game people can understand. Turn "Share play data" off in Settings at any time: that stops it at once and deletes the install id and the queue on your device. A browser that sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track starts with it off. Kept 7 days on the server.

Reactions and watching. Which of the eight reactions your player id left on which run, and which recordings your player id watched and how often, with the times. Purpose: other players see the counts, never who left what or who watched. Both stay until you take the reaction back or delete your data.

Divisions and trophies. When a day closes, the division your checked game placed in, your place in it, any medal, and a running count of medals. Purpose: a board of your own size. Other players see the division board with your name, as they see the day's board. Your name comes off when you delete your data.

Daily reminder, only if you turn it on. The push subscription your browser issues (an address at your browser maker's push service and two keys that let only your browser read the message) and the hour you chose, with your player id when you have claimed a name. Purpose: one notification a day, "The yard is open", the same for everyone, nothing else. Legal basis: consent, withdrawn by turning the reminder off, which deletes the subscription; "Delete my data" removes it too, and a subscription the push service reports gone is dropped.
Not collected: no e-mail address, no password, no cookies, no advertising or analytics scripts, no payment data, no precise location. The desktop edition sends nothing the web game does not.

sections.title: How long
items: Entries and replays follow the fairness policy's retention: replays are kept for each seed's top 100 entries; 30 days after a daily closes it moves to cold storage, where every entry and the final board stay and only the top 10 replays remain; boards are kept 400 days back. Your name and group memberships stay until you delete them.

Play-statistics events: 7 days. Logs: by rotation, as above. Nightly backups of the verifier's data are kept for 14 days, so a record you deleted can survive in a backup for up to 14 days before it is gone everywhere; backups are used to recover from a failure, never to restore a deleted player.

sections.title: Who else sees it
items: Processors that run the service for the operator: Hetzner Online GmbH (virtual server in the European Union); Cloudflare, Inc. (Pages hosting, DNS and e-mail forwarding for the domain); GitHub, Inc. (source code, releases, the desktop installer); Let's Encrypt (TLS certificates for the verifier's host name); Discord Inc. (only when the operator connects a channel: open and close announcements and new #1 scores, the same facts the public board shows).

Your browser connects to Cloudflare's network to load the game and to the verifier's host to submit runs and read boards; each sees your network address the way any web server does, under its own privacy policy. The verifier itself stores no addresses.

The boards are public. Anyone can see your display name and tag, your scores and ranks and, within the fairness policy's reveal rules, your replays; a Discord channel the operator connects shows the same facts. Nothing is sold, and there is no advertising.

If you turn the daily reminder on, your browser maker's push service (Apple, Google or Mozilla, depending on the browser) relays one encrypted message a day: it sees that a message went to your browser, not what it says.

sections.title: Where
items: The verifier runs in the European Union. The operator lives in the United States and reaches the data from there to run the service. Cloudflare serves the game from the location nearest to you.

sections.title: Your rights
items: Download everything stored under your player id: "Download my data" in the game (Privacy & data), or GET /me/export with your key. The file lists your entries with their replays where kept, your group memberships, the moderation record of your name and the reports you filed.

Delete it: "Delete my data" in the game, or DELETE /me with your key. Your name is removed, your entries stay on the boards anonymised as "deleted" with the score only, their replays are dropped from live and cold storage, your group memberships end, and the key on your device is replaced, so nothing links the old entries to you.
Correct it: the player button renames you (once every 24 hours); turning play statistics off ends that processing at once.

Object to or ask about anything here at contact@junkyarddraft.com. Because the verifier knows you only by the hash of your device key, a request about a specific player has to come from the device that holds the key or from its recovery code: by e-mail alone we cannot tell whose data is whose, and we will not guess.
If you live in the EU, the EEA or the UK you may also complain to your data protection authority; elsewhere, to the body responsible for privacy where you live.

sections.title: Children
items: The game is not directed at children under 13 and collects no personal information to play. Display names are public: do not use a real name, and if you are under 13 do not claim a name or turn play statistics on.

sections.title: Changes
items: The date at the top changes with the text, and every change is listed in the repository's changelog at https://github.com/blickz55/junkyard-draft. The fairness policy, generated from the code, describes the exact rules, limits and retention in force and is part of this notice.

docs.title: Terms of play
docs.summary: Junkyard Draft is a free game with public, verified leaderboards, run by one person on a small budget. Play fair, choose a name fit for a public board, keep your recovery code private. The service is best-effort: it may change, pause or stop.

sections.title: The service
items: Junkyard Draft is a free browser and desktop game operated by Jon (GitHub: blickz55). Playing needs no account. Submitting a run to the verified boards, claiming a display name, joining a group and reporting a name are the interactions with the service, and these terms govern them. By submitting a run or claiming a name you accept these terms, the community guidelines and the fairness policy, which is generated from the code and is part of these terms.

sections.title: Your key and your name
items: Your device creates a key on first use. Whoever holds it, or its recovery code, is you to the verifier: keep the code private. A lost key cannot be recovered and we cannot tell who used one. One key is one player; holding several places on a board with several keys is not allowed.

Display names and group names follow the community guidelines: no impersonation, no slurs, no personal information, nothing that misleads about the game's staff. You may rename once every 24 hours; a rename follows you onto every board.

sections.title: What "verified" means
items: A verified score means the verifier re-simulated the submitted replay with the stated rules version and reached the same result, and that the submission arrived inside the event's window. It does not certify that a human played without tools: the game is deterministic and its source is open, so anyone can compute a good run. The boards rank verified replays; the fairness policy describes ties, retention and medals.

Rules versions change. When a rule or a tuning value changes, older replays stop verifying and the entries verified under the old version stay in their own archive. The daily secret, the limits and the schedule may change too.

sections.title: Fair play
items: Automated play on a ranked board (the daily, the weekly), exploiting a verifier bug to record a score the rules would not allow, and publishing an open daily's layout so others can copy it are breaches. Practice seeds, forks and challenges are yours to experiment on.

The operator may remove or anonymise entries, reset a board whose scores a bug produced, block a player id or an address range, and refuse submissions. When a whole board is affected the reason is stated where that board is shown. The autoplayer's par is a target line, never a competitor.

sections.title: Moderation
items: A name reported by 2 established players, or confirmed by a moderator, is shown as "player" on every board until it is reviewed; a moderator may rename a player or a group, clear a report or confirm a hide. Moderation never touches scores, and a report is never a ban. Appeals: moderation@junkyarddraft.com, with your tag.

sections.title: Your content
items: Display names, group names and the anonymous label are the only text you can enter. You allow the operator to show them on the boards, in the archive, in share cards other players make and in Discord announcements, and to filter or change them under the guidelines. The replays you submit may be shown to other players under the fairness policy's reveal rules and are kept as its retention rules describe.

sections.title: Availability and liability
items: This is an independent project. The service is provided as is, with no promise of uptime, of keeping boards or scores, or of continuing. It may change or stop. After a failure the boards may be rebuilt from a backup up to 14 days old.

To the extent the law allows, the operator is not liable for lost scores, lost time or indirect damage. Nothing here limits a liability that cannot be limited by law, and nothing here removes protections you have as a consumer where you live.

sections.title: The software
items: The game's source is published at https://github.com/blickz55/junkyard-draft under the licence in its LICENSE file: read it, run it, change it for yourself, contribute back. The name "Junkyard Draft", the art and the sounds are reserved, and no public instance may be run under the name. The desktop installer is unsigned and is distributed only through the repository's releases.

sections.title: Law and changes
items: These terms are governed by the law of the United States, without affecting mandatory protections where you live. They were last changed on 2026-10-30; changes are listed in the repository's changelog. If one clause turns out invalid, the rest stands.

docs.title: Community guidelines (v0)
docs.summary: The short version: be someone the other players want on the same board. These guidelines govern names, play on the ranked boards, sharing, groups and reports; they grow with the social features.

sections.title: Names
items: Pick a handle, not a real name, yours or anyone else's. No slurs, no sexual content, no harassment aimed at a person or a group, no impersonation of other players, of the game's staff or of a brand. Look-alike characters are folded before the blocklist is checked, so a disguised word is still the word. Group names follow the same rule. 32 characters at most.

sections.title: Play
items: Ranked boards are for runs you played yourself, in the game. Do not automate the daily or the weekly, do not feed replays from a solver, do not hold several places with several keys. Practice seeds, forks and challenges are the place to experiment. The par line is a bot: a target, not a person to outrank.

sections.title: Found an exploit?
items: A trick the simulation allows is a rule: use it, and tell us if it looks unintended. A way to make the verifier accept something the simulation would not is a bug: do not use it on a ranked board; report it to contact@junkyarddraft.com and get credit in the changelog.

sections.title: Sharing
items: Share cards, challenge links and clips exist to be shared. On an open daily share your result, not your layout: the reveal rules hide replays until the day closes so that nobody copies a line, and posting a layout defeats them.

sections.title: Groups
items: A group code is an invitation: anyone who has it can join and see the group's boards, so post it where you want everyone reading to join. The creator may rename or disband a group; leaving is always possible.

sections.title: Reporting
items: Report a name from any board or replay with one of the fixed reasons. Reports are counted, not read as text: 2 established players agreeing hide a name until a moderator looks. Do not report scores you dislike, and do not organise mass reports: that is itself a breach.

sections.title: Consequences and appeals
items: In order of weight: a hidden name, a forced rename, removal of entries, a block. Appeals go to moderation@junkyarddraft.com with your tag; a moderator answers within a week where possible, best-effort.

sections.title: Discord and other places
items: If the operator runs a Discord server or another community space, these guidelines apply there as well, together with that platform's own rules.
